# isHtmlOutput

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is an HtmlOutput.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isHtmlOutput() — Checks whether a value is an HtmlOutput. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/ui</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isHtmlOutput(value: unknown): value is HtmlOutput;
```

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard looks for the methods that define the type — `getContent`, `setTitle`, `setXFrameOptionsMode`. A stub that implements them passes, which is what makes code using this guard testable outside the runtime.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is an HtmlOutput; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `HtmlOutput` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const output = HtmlService.createHtmlOutput("<p>hi</p>");

isHtmlOutput(output); // => true
isHtmlOutput({}); // => false
isHtmlOutput(null); // => false
```
